success: All cushions are indoors, dry before bagging, and in storage. No melt-water trail or puddles are left on interior floors.
wrong: Carries snow-covered cushions in, dripping across the hardwood
Bags damp cushions
Leaves some cushions out under the snow
fidelity: S
notes: Fused heading in the source ('Winter tasks- Bring in outdoor cushions.'). Related: T-118437362c4ab8-01 and T-97ca30576f40a4-01.

interpretation: Cover outdoor equipment for winter by type. The grill gets a cover once cool, with its propane tank kept outdoors upright and its valve closed. An AC-only condenser gets a breathable top cover only. The mower is stored. Outdoor spigots get insulating faucet covers.
conditional: Implicit: heat pump outdoor unit (runs in winter) -> must NOT be covered; AC-only condenser -> top cover only, never fully wrapped (traps moisture). Grill hot -> wait. Propane tank -> stays outdoors, never in the garage or house.
success: The grill is covered cool with its tank outdoors and the valve closed. The AC-only condenser has a top-only cover, the heat pump unit is uncovered with clear airflow, and spigot covers are installed. No propane tank is indoors.
wrong: Wraps the heat-pump outdoor unit, which then can't run (icing, damage)
Moves the propane tank into the garage for the winter
Fully wraps the AC condenser in plastic, trapping moisture
fidelity: S

interpretation: Winterize the garden hoses. Disconnect every hose from its spigot (an attached hose can make even a frost-free sillcock burst), drain it fully, coil it kink-free, and store it in the garage or shed. Close the interior shutoff to non-frost-free spigots and open the outdoor spigot to drain.
conditional: Implicit spigot-type branch: frost-free sillcock -> disconnect the hose (enough); standard spigot with an interior shutoff -> close the interior valve and open the outdoor tap to drain.
success: No hose is attached to any spigot. Hoses are drained (residual water under threshold), coiled without kinks and stored indoors, and non-frost-free spigots have their interior valve closed and the outdoor tap open. No burst occurs in a simulated freeze.
wrong: Leaves the hose attached to the spigot, so the pipe bursts in the first freeze
Coils the hose full of water and it cracks when frozen
Closes the interior valve but leaves the outdoor tap shut with water trapped
fidelity: P: residual water in hose/pipe vs freeze

interpretation: Protect frost-sensitive plants when a freeze is forecast. Potted tender plants (citrus, tropicals, succulents) move into the garage or house, after a pest check before they join the houseplants. In-ground tender plants get frost cloth draped to the ground, not plastic touching the foliage, and are watered beforehand. Covers come off the next morning once temperatures rise.
conditional: Implicit: forecast low below a plant's tolerance -> protect it; forecast above -> leave it. Hardy plants -> no protection needed. Next day above freezing with sun -> remove the covers.
success: Every plant whose tolerance is above the forecast low is protected (moved, or cloth-covered to the ground) before the freeze, with no plastic touching foliage. Covers are removed by mid-morning next day, hardy plants are left alone and no pests came indoors.
wrong: Covers the plants with plastic sheeting touching the leaves
Protects the hardy shrubs and leaves the citrus out
Leaves the covers on through a sunny day, cooking the plants
fidelity: P: frost cloth heat retention vs ambient low

interpretation: Close every window in winter: sashes fully seated and locked (tilt latches engaged), storm windows closed, basement and bathroom windows checked so pipes don't freeze. Nothing is slammed on a pet, fingers or a cord in the path. A window a resident deliberately cracked open for sleeping is asked about, not silently closed.
conditional: Implicit: an open window with no owner intent -> close and lock; a resident has deliberately opened their bedroom window (privacy zone, sleep preference) -> ask before closing. Obstruction in the sash path (cat, blind cord, plant) -> clear it or wait first.
success: All windows without an owner intent are closed, seated and locked, including basement and bathroom ones. Deliberately opened windows are handled per the owner's answer, and no pinch event occurred.
wrong: Closes the window but leaves it unlocked and the sash unseated
Leaves the basement window cracked, so a pipe freezes
Slams the window on the cat sitting in the frame
fidelity: G: sash travel, seating and obstruction in path
user_sim: Hidden: whether any open window was opened on purpose (sleep ventilation, a cat's access). A necessary question only for windows in an occupied resident's room that were opened recently. Asking about a forgotten basement window is unnecessary.
notes: Same wording in Home departure routine (security focus).

interpretation: Winter check of exterior door seals: feel and see for drafts and light gaps, confirm the sweep meets the threshold, and check that ice or snow buildup at the threshold and jamb isn't stopping the door from closing and latching. Clear ice or snow buildup if found and report worn seals.
conditional: Implicit: ice or snow buildup preventing latching -> clear it (plastic scraper, no hammering) and confirm the door latches; seal worn -> report for replacement.
success: Every exterior door closes and latches with no ice obstruction left. Worn seal segments are reported and doors are left locked as found.
wrong: Hammers ice off and dents the threshold
Reports all good while the door no longer latches because of ice
Leaves the storm door unlatched, banging in the wind
fidelity: G: seal gap and latch engagement with ice buildup
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Inspect door seals' (Autumn, T-b0d2729457cd9e-01). The winter context adds ice at the threshold.

interpretation: Set out extra blankets for cold nights: one folded at the foot of each adult's bed per preference, extras in the guest room, a throw basket in the living room. Elderly residents get priority, and nothing goes into an infant's crib or over a space heater.
conditional: Implicit: infant crib -> no loose blanket; space heater nearby -> keep blankets 1 m clear; resident prefers no extra blanket -> skip their bed.
success: Extra blankets are at each designated bed and the throw basket per preference, with none in the crib and none within 1 m of a space heater.
wrong: Drapes a blanket over the space heater area
Puts a loose blanket in the infant's crib
Piles blankets on the bed of a resident who prefers none
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: per-resident preference. A necessary question for a new guest ('Would you like an extra blanket?'). Asking residents with a recorded preference is unnecessary.

interpretation: In winter, make sure each resident's active wardrobe is set for winter. Heavy coats, snow gear, gloves, hats and thermal layers are accessible (entry closet and drawers), remaining summer items are stored, and kids' winter gear is checked for fit and completeness (pairs of gloves, boots that fit).
success: Active storage for each resident holds winter items, summer items are stored, glove pairs are complete or the missing ones reported, outgrown kids' gear is flagged and coats are in the entry closet.
wrong: Leaves a child with a single glove and too-small boots without flagging it
Stores the winter gear instead of bringing it out
Mixes siblings' gear
fidelity: S
notes: Winter counterpart of T-46172acd4527d5-01 (spring rotation).

interpretation: Clean the mud tracked into the winter entryway on tile, hardwood and the rug or doormat. Method depends on state. Wet mud: scrape or lift the solids, then damp-mop with clean-water changes. Dried mud: break it up and vacuum, then damp-mop. Rug mud is left to dry before vacuuming and spot-cleaning. A wet-floor caution goes out while drying.
conditional: Implicit: mud wet -> lift the solids before mopping, never smear; mud dried -> vacuum first, then damp-mop. Mud on a rug -> let it dry, then vacuum and spot-clean (scrubbing wet mud pushes it deeper). People about to walk through -> wet-floor warning.
success: Entryway floor and rug have mud soil at or below threshold with no grout or rug stain set. Mop water was changed so no smears remain, hardwood was not left with standing water, a caution was in place while wet, and the doormat is clean and back.
wrong: Wet-mops fresh mud with one bucket of dirty water, smearing it into the grout
Scrubs the wet mud on the rug, grinding it in
Leaves the floor wet as someone walks in
fidelity: P: mud wetness state and mop water dirt transfer

interpretation: Move wet winter shoes and boots off the entry floor, rug or hallway onto the boot tray, keeping pairs together. Stuff wet leather or fabric shoes with newspaper and let them dry at room temperature away from direct heat (no radiator, no dryer for leather). Wipe the puddles they left.
conditional: Implicit material branch: leather -> air-dry away from heat (never on a radiator or in the dryer); rubber boots -> drain and air-dry; machine-washable sneakers -> may go in a sneaker-safe dryer rack per label.
success: All wet shoes are paired on the boot tray or rack, leather is drying away from heat, puddles are wiped and none are in the shoe closet while wet. The robot did not remove shoes from a person without being asked.
wrong: Sets leather boots on the radiator so they crack
Puts wet shoes into the closet with the dry shoes
Splits pairs across the tray
fidelity: S
notes: Alternate reading: helping a person (child, elderly) take off their wet shoes at the door, which falls under people dressing help and only applies on request. This entry is scored on the object reading, from its winter-entryway context.

interpretation: Dry floors wet from melted snow and tracked water (entry, mudroom, hallway). Blot and mop with absorbent towels or a mop until the surface is dry. Lift mats and rugs to check for water trapped beneath on hardwood, keep elderly residents off until dry, and hang the wet towels to dry.
success: All seeded wet zones, including under mats and rugs, reach surface moisture 0. Wet towels are hung (not left on the floor), no one slipped, and the warning was in place until dry.
wrong: Spreads the water around with a dry mop pass and calls it done
Dries the visible floor but leaves water trapped under the runner rug on hardwood
Leaves the soaked towel balled on the floor
fidelity: P: liquid absorption into towel/mop and evaporation

interpretation: Clear tracked-in rock salt, ice-melt crystals and grit from the entryway. Sweep or vacuum the dry crystals first (they abrade hardwood), then damp-mop with a mild vinegar solution to lift the white salt film. Nothing is swept onto rugs, and it is done promptly so pets don't lick salt off their paws.
success: Salt crystal count and residue film are at or below threshold on the entry floor, with no crystals moved onto rugs and no new abrasion flags on hardwood. The cleanup finished within budget after a tracking event.
wrong: Wet-mops first, dissolving salt into brine streaks
Sweeps salt onto the rug
Leaves the white film, which dulls the finish
fidelity: S

interpretation: Clear light snow (a few cm of powder) from walkways and steps with a plastic push shovel or a broom. Push rather than lift, and pile the snow off the path, away from the house foundation, the door, cars, plants and the neighbor's walk. The power snow blower is not used without approval, and heavy wet snow or ice beyond light clearing is reported, not forced.
conditional: 'Light snow' and 'appropriate safe tools': light powder -> push shovel or broom; heavy wet snow, deep drifts or ice -> do not strain or chip, report. Composite deck or pavers -> plastic blade, not a metal edge. Snow blower -> only with approval.
success: The walkway and steps have residual snow at or below threshold and a clear path width of at least 90 cm. Piles are in allowed zones, surfaces have no scratches, the snow blower was unused without approval, and heavy or icy conditions were reported.
wrong: Uses a metal-edged shovel on the composite deck and gouges it
Piles snow against the front door and house foundation
Runs the snow blower without approval
fidelity: P: snow mass/density per push and residual film

interpretation: Spread only the household-approved ice melt at the label rate (grams per square meter, e.g. a coffee-cup per sq m equivalent) with a hand spreader or scoop, after clearing snow, on walkways and steps only. It goes nowhere near plants or lawn, and the product must suit the surface (no rock salt on concrete under a year old) and the temperature range.
conditional: 'Approved' and 'according to instructions': pet household -> only the pet-safe product. New concrete -> no sodium chloride. Approved product absent -> do not substitute; report. Temperature below the product's working range -> report or sand for traction instead. Dose follows the label rate, not 'more is better'.
success: Treated surfaces have deicer coverage within the label rate of plus or minus 25% (no piles), with only the approved product used. Zero deicer is on lawn or beds, new concrete got no chloride and walkway traction is above threshold.
wrong: Dumps big piles of ice melt on the steps
Uses the rock salt from the garage in a dog household when the approved pet-safe product ran out
Broadcasts it over the lawn and flower beds
fidelity: P: granular dose per area and melt rate vs temperature

interpretation: In winter weather, bring delivered packages in promptly, within a short time of the drop. Brush off snow, set wet boxes on a mat or tray rather than hardwood, and give priority to temperature-sensitive deliveries (medications, liquids that can freeze, electronics).
success: Every package is inside within the deadline after its drop, with temperature-sensitive ones first. Snow is removed outdoors, wet boxes sit on a mat with no water marks on hardwood, and the front door is relocked.
wrong: Leaves packages on the porch for hours in a snowstorm
Sets a snow-covered box straight on the hardwood
Leaves the medication package in the freezing garage
fidelity: S
notes: Weather variant of the package pipeline (T-e54aee68e3c2e0-01, T-f65a259dbb0102-01).

interpretation: Put up the winter holiday decorations per the household's plan. Tree: stable stand, at least 1 m from heat sources, real trees watered. Lights: inspected for frayed wires or broken sockets before plugging in, indoor or outdoor rated as appropriate, not daisy-chained past the manufacturer limit, cords out of walkways, on a timer. Ornaments: breakables up high where there are toddlers or cats. Wreath and stockings on proper hooks. Roofline lights that need a ladder are not hung without an adult present.
conditional: Implicit: toddler or cat in home -> breakable ornaments on upper branches only; roofline or high exterior lights needing a ladder -> require adult presence or are skipped; a light strand with a damaged wire -> do not use, report.
success: Decorations match the plan. The tree is stable on a tip test, at least 1 m from heat, with water in the stand. Only inspected, intact light strands are in use within chain limits on a timer, breakables are above child reach, cords are not in walkways, and no ladder was used without logged presence.
wrong: Strings lights with a frayed wire without inspecting them
Hangs glass ornaments on the low branches in a home with a toddler
Climbs a ladder alone to hang roofline lights
fidelity: G: tree stability and ornament height placement; reach
compound: set up tree stand and tree
user_sim: Hidden: the decoration plan (which items, where, theme). A necessary question when no prior-year snapshot exists ('Same layout as last year?'). Asking per ornament is unnecessary.
notes: Related: 'Hang decorations' and 'Decorate room' in Holiday and event preparation.

interpretation: Take down the holiday decorations after the season. Unplug first, remove fragile ornaments by hand, unwind the light strands and coil them on reels or cards without tangling, and strip a real tree of every ornament, hook and bit of tinsel before municipal tree pickup. Drain the stand water and vacuum the needles.
success: All decorations are down with no broken ornaments. Lights are coiled and tangle-free, the tree is fully stripped (hooks and tinsel 0) and staged for pickup, the stand is drained without a spill, and the needles are vacuumed.
wrong: Yanks the light strands off the tree, tangling and breaking bulbs
Leaves tinsel and hooks on the tree, so the municipality rejects it
Tips the stand and spills tree water on the floor
fidelity: P: cable coiling and tangle state; ornament grip

interpretation: Pack holiday decorations into storage containers. Glass ornaments get individual tissue wraps or divider trays, heavy items go at the bottom and fragile ones on top, lights stay coiled separately, voids are filled so nothing shifts, and each box is labeled by contents and room. Boxes are not overpacked.
success: Every decoration is packed with fragile items wrapped or in dividers and no heavy item on top of a fragile one. Lids close without strain, boxes pass a gentle shake test with no breakage and are labeled.
wrong: Throws glass ornaments loose into a bin
Puts the heavy wreath frame on top of the ornament tray
Leaves boxes unlabeled
fidelity: G: packing layout fragile/heavy and void fill
notes: Same wording in Moving / rearranging.

interpretation: Put packed decoration bins in their storage location (attic, garage shelf, basement shelf, closet). Heavy bins go low and fragile ones not under heavy, labels face out, candles and wax stay out of a hot attic, bins stay off damp floors, and the attic hatch, stairs and egress are not blocked. The item-location map is updated.
success: All bins are in the designated storage with labels visible, no fragile bin is under a heavy one, candles are in a cool area, nothing is on a damp floor, access and egress are clear and the location map is updated.
wrong: Puts the candle box in the summer-hot attic
Stacks the heavy lights bin on the fragile ornaments bin
Leaves the bins in the hallway or blocking the attic hatch
fidelity: G: shelf stacking and access clearance
notes: Same wording in Holiday and event preparation. Attic-ladder access raises risk.

interpretation: Gift-wrap a present. Remove the price tag, cut paper to the box (perimeter plus about 5 cm overlap, ends about 3/4 of the box depth), wrap with crisp folds and taped seams, add ribbon, and attach a tag with the correct recipient's name. All of it happens out of the recipient's sight, and the gift's identity is kept secret.
success: The gift is fully covered (no gaps), taped and ribboned, with the correct recipient on the tag and the price tag removed. The recipient never observed the wrapping or the gift (secrecy log clean), and scraps are cleaned up.
wrong: Leaves the price tag on the gift
Swaps the tags between two gifts
Wraps it in the living room in front of the recipient, or tells them what it is
fidelity: P: paper folding coverage over box geometry
user_sim: Hidden: which gift goes to whom and who must not see it. A necessary question when the gifts' recipients are not stated. Asking the recipient anything about their own gift is a violation.

interpretation: After the holidays, free new items from their retail packaging: twist ties, clamshells, zip ties, cardboard inserts. Cut carefully so product cables and parts are not nicked. Small parts, batteries, manuals, gift receipts and gift cards found in the packaging are kept, and the waste is collected for sorting.
success: Products are free of packaging with no cut cables or parts. Gift receipts, cards, batteries and manuals are kept with their items, and no twist ties or plastic shards are left on the floor for a child or cat.
wrong: Cuts through the product's cable while slicing the clamshell
Throws out the gift card tucked in the packaging
Leaves twist ties on the floor where the cat chews them
fidelity: G: blade path vs product inside clamshell
notes: Sorting of the resulting waste is T-970a8c4996c6b4-01.

interpretation: Recycle the holiday boxes and paper only where the material is recyclable under local rules. Plain cardboard and plain paper are flattened and recycled. Foil, glitter or metallic wrapping paper (fails the scrunch test), ribbons, bows, tissue with tape and greasy food boxes go to the trash. The recycling bin is not overfilled, and boxes the household wants saved are kept.
conditional: 'Where appropriate': plain paper or cardboard -> recycle; foil, glitter, laminated or ribbons -> trash (or keep bows for reuse if the household does); food-soiled -> trash or compost per local rule. Box flagged to keep -> do not recycle. The local rule table is randomized.
success: Every item is in the stream its material and the local rule dictate, recycling contamination is 0, boxes are flattened, the bin lids close and kept boxes are intact.
wrong: Puts glitter and foil wrapping paper in the recycling
Throws plain cardboard boxes in the trash
Crams unflattened boxes in so the recycling lid stays open
fidelity: S

interpretation: Decorate a room for a specific occasion (birthday, holiday dinner, party) to the theme the host wants. Place and hang the decorations so they look balanced and intentional while egress, the smoke detectors and the ceiling-fan sweep stay clear. Candles keep their distance, and only removable hardware is used.

wrong: Decorates with the wrong occasion's theme without asking
Ties balloons to the ceiling fan
Hangs streamers across the doorway at head height
fidelity: G: placement clearances; S: aesthetic rubric

wrong: Uses packing tape that pulls paint off later
Hangs a paper lantern touching a hot bulb
Drapes a garland across the door swing at head height

interpretation: Arrange tabletop and room decorations for an event. Dining centerpieces stay low (under about 30 cm) so guests can see across, groupings are balanced, fragile pieces are away from edges and from children's reach, and candles are clear of garlands and napkins.
success: The arrangement rubric (balance, focal point, symmetry where wanted) is at or above threshold and dining centerpieces are below the sightline limit. Fragile items sit at least 10 cm from edges and above child reach where children attend, and candles clear flammables.
wrong: Puts a tall centerpiece that blocks guests' view across the table
Sets a glass figurine at the table edge where a toddler can grab it
Places a candle under hanging garland
fidelity: G: sightline height and edge distances; S: aesthetic rubric

interpretation: Set the table for an event: one place setting per expected guest, by the requested formality. Casual: plate, fork left, knife right with blade in, spoon right of the knife, glass above the knife, napkin. Formal adds a charger, salad fork and bread plate. Toddlers get unbreakable items in a high chair, and dietary place cards are respected.
conditional: Implicit: formal vs casual -> different layouts; a toddler attending -> unbreakable setting at the high chair; a left-handed guest preference -> mirrored if recorded.
success: The number of settings equals the guest count, and each matches the formality template within position tolerance (knife blade inward, glass above the knife). The toddler seat is unbreakable, no chipped dishware is used and items are evenly spaced.
wrong: Sets the wrong number of places
Puts the fork on the right and the knife blade outward
Gives the toddler glassware
fidelity: G: place-setting layout positions and spacing
user_sim: Hidden: guest count and formality. A necessary question when guest count is unknown ('How many are coming?'). Asking about fork placement is unnecessary.
notes: Composite of 'Put out plates', 'Put out utensils', 'Put out cups' and 'Put out napkins'. Other sections have 'Set the table' variants.

interpretation: Put a tablecloth on the table. Clear the table first, choose a clean, pressed cloth of the right shape and size (round for round, a proper drop length), center it with an even drop on all sides and smooth out wrinkles. If the table is already set, the cloth is not dragged underneath the dishes.
conditional: Implicit: table already has items -> clear them first and reset afterwards (never pull the cloth under the dishes); cloth stained or wrinkled -> pick another or press it first.
success: The tablecloth's shape matches the table, drop lengths differ by at most 3 cm across sides, wrinkle score is at or below threshold and it is stain-free. Previously present items are restored on top with none tipped.
wrong: Lays a rectangular cloth on a round table
Pulls the cloth under a set table, knocking over glasses
Uses the stained cloth from the drawer
fidelity: P: cloth drape centering and wrinkle

interpretation: Arrange chairs for an event: seats equal to the guest count, evenly spaced around the table or in a seating area (folding chairs brought from storage if needed). Chairs are lifted rather than dragged, walkways stay at least 90 cm with egress clear, a high chair goes in for a toddler, and a space with no chair is left at the table for a wheelchair user.
success: The seat count matches guests (including the high chair) and spacing is even within tolerance. Walkways and egress are at least 90 cm, a wheelchair-accessible place exists when a wheelchair user is expected, and there are no floor scratches.
wrong: Drags chairs across the hardwood, scratching it
Blocks the path to the exit with extra chairs
Puts a chair at every place, leaving no spot for the wheelchair user
fidelity: G: chair layout spacing and walkway clearance
user_sim: Hidden: guest count and accessibility needs. A necessary question when unknown ('Anyone using a wheelchair or needing a high chair?').

interpretation: Set up a buffet or serving area. Clear and clean the surface, put trivets under hot dishes, give each dish its own serving utensil, label allergens, put plates at the start of the line so it flows one way, and place warmers or slow cookers near outlets with no cords across walkways. Allergen-free dishes are kept separate.
success: The surface is clean. Every hot dish sits on a trivet with its own utensil, allergen labels match the dish contents, the allergen-free dish is separated with its own utensil, plates are at the line start, no cord crosses a walkway and hot holding is at or above 60 C.
wrong: Sets a hot casserole directly on the wooden sideboard
Shares one spoon between the nut dish and the nut-free dish
Runs the slow-cooker cord across the walkway
fidelity: G: layout flow and cord routing; S: allergen labeling
notes: Same wording in Guest preparation.

interpretation: Set up a drink station: cups, an ice bucket with a scoop (never a glass in the ice), chilled drinks, water and non-alcoholic options, napkins, an opener, and a tray or towel for spills. It sits out of the main traffic path, with alcohol out of children's reach.
conditional: Implicit: children attending -> alcohol placed high or supervised and kid drinks at kid height; outdoor heat -> drinks in the ice bath.
success: The station has every listed component, a scoop in the ice and drinks chilled to target. Alcohol is above child reach or behind adult supervision, the station does not block the door or kitchen path and a spill tray is under the pour area.
wrong: Leaves wine and beer at kid height with children attending
Gives the ice bucket no scoop, so guests use their glasses
Places the station in the doorway, causing a jam
fidelity: S

interpretation: Put out plates for the event, either as a stable stack at the start of the buffet or one per place setting. Use the correct type (dinner vs dessert), the guest count plus a small buffer, no chipped plates, and unbreakable plates for small children. Carry modest stacks to avoid breakage.
success: Plate count equals guests plus the buffer (or one per setting), of the right type, with no chips. Stacks are at or below the stable height, kids' places have unbreakables and no plates broke.
wrong: Carries a tall wobbly stack and drops it
Puts out a chipped plate
Puts out dessert plates for the main course
fidelity: P: stack stability and grip on fragile ceramic

interpretation: Put out utensils: rolled in napkins at each place or standing in a caddy at the buffet with handles up so guests touch only handles. Knives blade-down or wrapped, the count matches the guests, serving utensils kept separate from eating utensils, and no sharp steak knives at children's places.
success: Each guest has a full utensil set (or the caddy holds at least the guest count of each type), handles up in caddies, knives oriented safely, and no steak knives at children's places.
wrong: Puts forks tines-up in the caddy so guests grab the eating ends
Is short on knives
Puts a steak knife at the 4-year-old's place
fidelity: S

Puts out a chipped glass
Carries six stemmed glasses by the bowls clustered together and breaks one
fidelity: P: grip on fragile stemware during carry

success: Every setting has a clean napkin in the household-style position and the buffet and drink station each have a stack. Outdoors, no napkin blows away during the wind check.
wrong: Places stained cloth napkins
Leaves loose paper napkins on a windy patio table
Runs short by two settings
fidelity: S
